title: A data file read into records

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the report here; it reads sailings.csv and writes report.txt beside it.

tasks.title: Read one line into a record
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1`, write a class `Lines` with one method. `static Sailing parse(String line, int number)` gives back the `Sailing` a line such as `2031-06-14,Linnet,23,77.05` holds: the date, the boat, the number of passengers and the takings, split at the commas, each part with any space at either end left off. A line that cannot be read, because it has not exactly four parts or a part is not what it should be, throws an `IllegalArgumentException` whose message names `number`, the line's number. `Sailing` is given above the tasks.

Check calls `parse` with lines of its own, some with spaces around their parts and some that cannot be read, and reads the `Sailing` it gets back, or an exception by its type and whether its message names the number.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about reading one line.
Split the line, and count its parts before reading any of them.
Read each part with the tool for its type: a date, a whole number, an amount.
Catch what reading a bad part throws, and throw what the task asks for in its place.
hints: Each part of the line is text, and each earlier issue of this part showed how to read one kind of text: a date, an amount. A whole number comes from text as it did in part 5.
The exceptions that reading a bad part throws name the part, never the line. One catch around all the reading can throw a new exception whose message holds the number, with the old one as its cause.

`String[] parts = line.split(",");`, refuse when `parts.length != 4`, then in a try: `new Sailing(LocalDate.parse(parts[0].strip()), parts[1].strip(), Integer.parseInt(parts[2].strip()), new BigDecimal(parts[3].strip()))`, and in its catch `throw new IllegalArgumentException("Line " + number + " cannot be read: " + line, e);`.

videos.title: Reading a CSV file into objects

tasks.title: Read the file, keep the good lines
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, write a class `Day` with one method, with `throws IOException`. `static List<Sailing> read(Path file, List<String> problems)` reads `file`, in UTF-8, and gives back a `Sailing` for each line after the first, which is the header, read with `Lines.parse`. A line is numbered as the file numbers it, the header being line 1. A line `parse` refuses is left out, its exception's message is added to `problems`, and the lines after it are still read.

Check hands `read` a path to a file of its own and a list for the problems, and runs it beside Check's own right `Lines`, so Task 2 passes or fails on its own lines. Its files have Windows line ends or none at the very end, bad lines in the middle and at the end, or only a header; one is not there, and that exception reaches the caller. Check compares the sailings as a list, in order, and reads the problems.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about reading a data file.
Read the file's lines, and start after the header.
Work out each line's number as the file counts it, and hand it to parse.
Catch a refusal around one line only, so the next line is still read.
hints: The list of a file's lines starts at position 0, and the file starts at line 1. The header is a line of the file, not a sailing.
A try around the whole loop stops at the first bad line; a try inside the loop deals with one line and goes on. What a caught exception says is its message.

`List<String> lines = Files.readAllLines(file, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);` then `for (int i = 1; i < lines.size(); i++)`, with `try { sailings.add(Lines.parse(lines.get(i), i + 1)); } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) { problems.add(e.getMessage()); }` inside it.

tasks.title: Add up the takings and write the report
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, write a class `Report` with two methods. `static BigDecimal takings(List<Sailing> sailings)` gives back the takings of all the sailings added up, and 0 for none. `static void write(Path file, List<Sailing> sailings, List<String> problems)`, with `throws IOException`, makes `file` hold the report and nothing else, in UTF-8, each line followed by `"\n"`: a line for each sailing, its date, boat, passengers and takings, as in `2031-06-14 Linnet 23 £77.05`, then `Total` and the takings added up, as in `Total £107.20`, then each problem after `Problem:` and a space. Every amount has a pound sign, two decimal places and a point.

Check hands `takings` sailings of its own and compares the total by its value. It hands `write` a path to a file it wrote first, with sailings and problems of its own, and reads the file back afterwards, byte for byte. It runs with the formats and the line end of a Windows computer in Germany, so an amount or a line end that follows the computer shows.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about writing the report.
Write takings as the money issue added up the till.
Write write: build the whole report in a StringBuilder, then write it in one go.
Run main and open report.txt in the editor.
hints: Everything this needs is from the issues before: adding amounts, printing one the same on every computer, building a text a line at a time, writing a file.
A record gives back each part with a method of its name. A date prints as year-month-day by itself. An amount needs its decimal places fixed before it is written, and every line its own "\n".

takings: `total = total.add(s.takings());` in a loop from `BigDecimal.ZERO`. In write, for each sailing `b.append(s.date()).append(' ').append(s.boat()).append(' ').append(s.passengers()).append(" £").append(s.takings().setScale(2, RoundingMode.HALF_UP).toPlainString()).append("\n");`, then the Total and Problem lines the same way, and `Files.writeString(file, b, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);`.
